security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline package names, and official Expo documentation links. I found no prompt injection, hidden execution, credential access, data exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent in the skill files.

static_findings.snippet: This regenerates the `ios` and `android` directories. Ensure the project is not a bare workflow app
- Clear the cocoapods cache for iOS: `cd ios && pod install --repo-update`
- Clear derived data for Xcode: `npx expo run:ios --no-build-cache`
- Clear the Gradle cache for Android: `cd android && ./gradlew clean`
- Enable React Compiler in SDK 54+ by adding `"experiments": { "reactCompiler": true }` to app.json
- Delete sdkVersion from `app.json` to let Expo manage it automatically
Check if there are any outdated patches in the `patches/` directory. Remove them if they are no long
- `experimentalImportSupport` is enabled by default in SDK +54.
- Review release notes for the target SDK version at https://expo.dev/changelog
- Expo webpack is deprecated, migrate to [Expo Router and Metro web](https://docs.expo.dev/router/mi
- Clear the Gradle cache for Android: `cd android && ./gradlew clean`

content.user_title: Upgrade Expo SDKs with Guided Checks
content.value_statement: Expo upgrades can break dependencies, native builds, and React patterns. This skill gives structured upgrade steps, checks, and migration notes for SDK 53 and SDK 54.
actual_capabilities: Lists core Expo SDK upgrade commands and dependency repair steps.
Provides cache cleanup guidance for managed and bare Expo workflows.
Summarizes SDK 53 New Architecture migration concerns.
Summarizes SDK 54 React 19 and React Compiler changes.
Identifies deprecated Expo packages and common replacements.
Highlights Metro, Postcss, and configuration cleanup after upgrades.
limitations: It does not inspect a project unless the agent reads local files separately.
It does not guarantee compatibility for every native module or custom plugin.
It may need newer Expo release notes for SDK versions beyond the included references.
Commands can modify dependencies and native project folders when executed.

use_cases.description: Create a checklist before moving an app to a newer Expo SDK version.

use_cases.title: Fix post-upgrade build issues
use_cases.description: Use cache cleanup, dependency repair, and prebuild notes after an upgrade fails.

use_cases.title: Review SDK 54 migrations
use_cases.description: Check React 19, React Compiler, and New Architecture changes before release testing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Upgrade Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning an Expo SDK upgrade.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an Expo SDK upgrade. Give me the main steps, checks, and risks before I run commands.

prompt_templates.title: Dependency Repair Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Project has dependency warnings after an upgrade.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Expo dependency upgrade issue. Explain which repair commands to run and what each command changes.

prompt_templates.title: SDK 54 Migration Review
prompt_templates.scenario: App is moving to Expo SDK 54.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Expo SDK 54 migration plan. Include React 19 changes, React Compiler setup, and New Architecture checks.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before shipping an upgraded app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release readiness checklist for this upgraded Expo app. Cover native modules, deprecated packages, caches, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: I need to upgrade an Expo app from SDK 52 to SDK 54.
output_examples.output: The response gives a staged upgrade checklist, required dependency checks, SDK 54 migration notes, and testing priorities for native features.

output_examples.input: My upgraded Expo app has iOS and Android build failures.
output_examples.output: The response separates managed and bare workflow fixes, explains cache cleanup options, and lists files or modules to review.

output_examples.input: Does SDK 54 require React Compiler changes?
output_examples.output: The response explains the compiler setting, required architecture assumptions, cleanup opportunities, and verification steps.

best_practices: Run upgrade commands on a clean branch with committed changes.
Review official Expo release notes for the exact target SDK.
Test camera, audio, video, navigation, and native modules after upgrading.
anti_patterns: Do not delete caches or native folders without understanding project workflow.
Do not skip dependency checks after changing Expo SDK versions.
Do not assume old React patterns remain ideal after SDK 54.

faq.question: What does this skill help upgrade?
faq.answer: It helps plan and troubleshoot Expo SDK upgrades for React Native apps.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an agent or developer may choose to execute.

faq.question: Does it cover Expo SDK 54?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes notes for React 19, React Compiler, and New Architecture changes.

faq.question: Can it fix native module incompatibilities?
faq.answer: It can guide investigation, but each native module still needs project-specific verification.

faq.question: Is it useful for bare workflow apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes iOS CocoaPods, Android Gradle, and native project cleanup notes.

faq.question: Should I still read Expo release notes?
faq.answer: Yes. Use this skill with official release notes for the target SDK version.
